# Experiment brief (pre-launch): retargeting campaign holdout

*The one-page plan a product DS writes before launch. Inputs come from the Criteo test itself (baseline rate, variance
reduction). Traffic and prices are assumptions and are marked as such.*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Hypothesis** | Showing retargeting ads to eligible users increases purchases (conversions) within 14 days, enough to pay for the impressions. |
| **Unit / split** | User (browser cookie), randomized at eligibility; 85% treatment / 15% holdout (the advertiser wants most users to see ads). |
| **Primary metric (OEC proxy)** | Conversion within 14 days. Baseline 0.194% (Criteo control). |
| **Secondary** | Site visit within 14 days (leading indicator, much more sensitive). |
| **Guardrails** | Opt-out / ad-blocking rate (non-inferiority, −2%); ad frequency per exposed user (cap); cost per exposed user from billing. *Not available in the public data.* |
| **Diagnostics (never decisive)** | Conversions per visit: its denominator is moved by the treatment. |
| **Analysis** | CUPAC on conversion (cross-fitted prediction from pre-period features), expected variance reduction 12.9%; BH across primary + secondary. |
| **Trust gates** | SRM χ² (p < 0.0005 → BLOCK); pre-period covariate balance (p < 0.001 → HOLD); A/A on the pipeline before launch. |

## Sample size and runtime (α = 0.05 two-sided, power 80%, 85/15 split)

| Minimum detectable effect (relative) | Users needed, raw | With CUPAC | Days at 500k new eligible users/day (assumed) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5% | 12,683,927 | 11,048,551 | 22.1 |
| 10% | 3,170,982 | 2,762,138 | 5.5 |
| 20% | 792,745 | 690,534 | 1.4 |

Plan: enroll for **14 days** (two weekly cycles) at an assumed 500,000 eligible users/day,
i.e. 7,000,000 users. That detects about 6.3% relative with CUPAC, comfortably below the 10%
design target; 5% would need 4.0× the users of the 10% design. Each user's
conversion window is 14 days, so the final read is on **day 28**. Whether an effect of a given size *pays*
depends on the cost per exposed user (break-even table in the [decision memo](decision_memo.md)).

## Stopping rule

O'Brien–Fleming (Lan–DeMets, two-sided form α(t) = 2 − 2Φ(1.96/√t)) with two looks: an interim read on day
21, when the first enrollment week's windows are complete (information ≈ 0.5), and the final read on day
28. Stop for benefit only if |z| exceeds 2.77 / 1.98.
(gsDesign's per-side convention gives slightly different bounds; both control α.) Stop for harm at any look if a
guardrail is significantly worse than its margin. The dashboard's daily p-value is not a stopping rule: on real ASOS
experiments, daily peeking flagged 218 of
361 metric trajectories, against
105 that were significant at the end.

## Decision rule (agreed before launch)

Ship (keep the campaign) if the primary metric is positive and significant after BH, all guardrails are within margin,
and the break-even condition holds at the CI lower bound: cost per exposed user < value per conversion × incremental
conversions per exposed user. HOLD on any trust-gate failure.
